subject: microbiology
title: Culture Media I: Basal, Enriched, Selective and Differential Media

steps.tx: **Nutrient agar** is the basal workhorse (peptone, meat extract, agar at neutral pH) growing non fastidious bacteria for colony study, its broth twin (nutrient broth) for turbidity cultures. Agar itself, from red algae via the Koch lesson, melts at 95 and sets at 42 degrees, inert nutrition wise, which is why this transparent jelly carries world microbiology without feeding it.
steps.say: Agar feeds nothing and carries everything; basal media grow the unfussy majority.

left.title: Basal media
points: Nutrient agar and broth: routine growth
Peptone water: indole and fermentation base
Agar properties: melts 95 C, sets 42 C, not metabolised

steps.tx: **Blood agar** enriches with 5 to 10 percent sheep blood and differentiates by haemolysis (alpha greenish partial, beta clear complete, gamma none), while **chocolate agar** heats the blood to burst red cells and release X and V factors for Haemophilus and Neisseria. Same ingredient, temperature decides the menu, the media kitchen's cleanest example.
steps.say: Heat the blood and chocolate agar feeds the fastidious; leave it whole and blood agar grades haemolysis.

left.title: Blood agar reads
points: Target haemolysis and double zones (C perfringens)

right.title: Chocolate agar
points: Lysed blood releases X (haemin) and V (NAD)
Bacitracin and factor discs refine identification

steps.tx: **Blood agar** is enriched with 5 to 10 percent sheep blood and also sorts colonies by haemolysis. Alpha haemolysis is a greenish partial clearing. Beta haemolysis is a fully clear zone. Gamma means no haemolysis at all. Heating the same blood bursts the red cells and releases X and V factors, producing chocolate agar for Haemophilus and Neisseria. Temperature, not a new ingredient, decides which fastidious organisms can grow. Leaving the blood whole grades streptococcal and other haemolysis. Heating it feeds species that cannot take intact red cells.
steps.say: Sheep blood agar, at 5 to 10 percent, both enriches growth and shows haemolysis: green partial alpha, clear complete beta, or none, called gamma. Heat that blood and it becomes chocolate agar, releasing X and V factors for Haemophilus and Neisseria. The ingredient is the same. The temperature sets the menu.

vis.alt: A blood agar plate shows greenish partial haemolysis, a fully clear zone, and colonies with no haemolysis at all.
vis.caption: Sheep blood agar displays partial green haemolysis, complete clear haemolysis, and no haemolysis side by side. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **MacConkey agar** selects gram negatives (bile salts and crystal violet exclude gram positives) and differentiates lactose fermenters (E coli pink by neutral red in acid) from non fermenters (Salmonella, Shigella pale), sorbitol MacConkey variant hunting E coli O157 by its sorbitol silence. One plate both gates and sorts stool flora, which is why it anchors enteric benches.
steps.say: Pink on MacConkey means lactose fermented; pale colonies from stool demand pathogen thinking.

left.title: MacConkey design
points: Bile salts and crystal violet: gram positive exclusion
Lactose fermenters pink, late fermenters slower

right.title: Enteric sorting
points: Salmonella and Shigella: pale, further media
Proteus: pale with swarming restrained by bile

steps.tx: **MacConkey agar** selects and sorts at once. Bile salts and crystal violet keep gram positive bacteria out. Neutral red turns lactose fermenters pink as they make acid, the usual colour of Escherichia coli. Salmonella and Shigella do not ferment lactose and stay pale. On sorbitol MacConkey, Escherichia coli O157 is the pale one, because it does not use sorbitol. Stool benches use that contrast because pathogens hide among a mass of pink normal flora.
steps.say: MacConkey agar blocks gram positives with bile salts and crystal violet, then colours lactose fermenters pink with neutral red. Escherichia coli is typically pink. Salmonella and Shigella stay pale. On sorbitol MacConkey, O157 stays pale because it does not ferment sorbitol. Pale colonies from stool need pathogen thinking.

vis.alt: A MacConkey agar plate shows pink lactose fermenting colonies beside pale colonies that have not fermented lactose.
vis.caption: Pink colonies have fermented lactose and turned neutral red, while pale colonies have not, on a plate that also suppresses gram positive growth. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Lowenstein Jensen medium** grows mycobacteria on inspissated egg with malachite green suppressing contaminants, glycerol favouring M tuberculosis (pyruvate variant for M bovis), colonies rough tough and buff in three to six weeks. Its slowness against MGIT liquid systems (next TB lessons) is generation time made visible on a slope.
steps.say: Egg, green dye and six weeks of patience: LJ is tuberculosis generation time in a bottle.

right.title: LJ discipline
points: Incubated up to 8 weeks before negative

steps.tx: **Loeffler serum slope** grows Corynebacterium diphtheriae rapidly with enhanced metachromatic granules for the Albert stain of the morphology lessons, while tellurite blood agar selects diphtheria bacilli as black colonies. Enrichment of a toxin producer's granules on serum medium is morphology scheduled by medium choice.
steps.say: Serum slopes fatten diphtheria granules for the stain that names them.

left.title: Diphtheria bench
points: Loeffler slope: rapid growth, granules enhanced
Albert stain: green bacilli, bluish black granules

steps.tx: **TCBS agar** (thiosulfate citrate bile sucrose) selects Vibrio cholerae at alkaline pH and reads sucrose: cholera yellow colonies, Vibrio parahaemolyticus green, most enterics suppressed by bile and alkalinity, with alkaline peptone water enrichment before it. Sucrose colour plus alkaline selection is cholera bench identity in one plate.
steps.say: Yellow on TCBS from rice water stool is cholera until excluded.

steps.tx: **Wilson Blair medium** (bismuth sulfite) selects Salmonella, Typhi classically, as black colonies with metallic sheen from hydrogen sulfide reducing bismuth, brilliant green suppressing coliforms, incubated longer (48 hours) than impatient benches prefer. XLD and Hektoen media share its stool Salmonella and Shigella stage with different indicator chemistries.
steps.say: Black metallic colonies on Wilson Blair pointed at typhi before serology spoke.

right.title: Stool plate partners
points: XLD: Salmonella black centres, Shigella red
Enrichment broths precede in carriers and food

steps.tx: **Medium taxonomy** consolidates for examinations: basal, enriched (blood added), selective (inhibitors), differential (indicators), enrichment (liquid favouring pathogens over rivals), transport (survival without multiplication), and anaerobic media, many plates serving two classes at once (MacConkey selective and differential). Classification questions ask the class and the ingredient that earns it.
steps.say: Name the ingredient and the class follows: bile selects, lactose indicator differentiates, blood enriches.

right.title: Liquid classes
points: Enrichment: selenite F, alkaline peptone water
